Storage place (Booking or Procedure) waits on OQ-93.
dataModelDeltas.verify_note: US-11.4.3 read in full: fields on the Booking, anaesthetist may change on the day, completion allowed without the number.

dataModelDeltas.title: The NHI is mandatory with no blank: a Booking cannot be saved without one, and an incoming row without one waits at intake
dataModelDeltas.catalogue_says: Every patient record has an NHI from creation, no blank and no pending state; one record per NHI. A Booking cannot be saved without one. An incoming booking (feed or surgeon PDF) with none waits on the matching screen's unmatched queue, creating neither Booking nor patient, until the office adds the NHI; waiting rows marked urgent as the date nears. A booking with no NHI may also show as a stub on its List: open (OQ-118, DM-58). Bookings searchable by NHI or name (US-11.1.1, US-11.1.4, US-11.1.5, US-02.1.4; OQ-49).
dataModelDeltas.prototype_has: Patient.nhi is optional (types.ts:173); upsertPatient creates a 'createdProvisional' record when no NHI is given (intake.ts:52); the UI prints 'NHI pending' (shared/format.ts:86). Dual-format validation (nhi.ts) fine. No waiting-row queue, no save guard, no search by NHI.
dataModelDeltas.impact: Patient.nhi becomes required; remove the provisional path and 'NHI pending' (16 non-test files read the NHI); creation paths refuse or park a row without one; waiting rows live in DM-34's queue; search by NHI or name. Seed patients need checking for blank NHIs.
dataModelDeltas.verify_note: Optional nhi and the provisional path confirmed in types.ts and intake.ts; reader count (16) re-grepped.

dataModelDeltas.title: A single Booking moves to a colleague by creating a List in the colleague's free Slot; whoever submits a List did its procedures
dataModelDeltas.catalogue_says: An anaesthetist can move a single Booking as well as a whole List, only to a colleague free in that Slot (scroll or type-to-filter), shown by availability alone, never ordered by tier or pairing (OQ-113, 29 Oct). The move creates a List in the colleague's Slot holding the Booking; never moved into an existing List; two Lists per Slot unsupported for now (OQ-85). A receiver on leave sets their Slot available first. Notices optional; no not-preferred warning. The List's anaesthetist did every procedure: a Booking done by someone else moves to a List of theirs and its payable follows; a prepaid Booking's payable is the AA Holding account, nothing moves or is recalculated, and the doer is paid by transfer.
dataModelDeltas.prototype_has: reassignBooking (lifecycle.ts:574) moves a Booking between Lists; an anaesthetist may only move between their own Lists ('notOwnList'), the office anywhere not AUTHORISED. Whole-List own move built (listMoveActions.ts:208,:222,:240); its colleague list is already flat (listMoves.ts:137). No single-Booking move, no creation of the receiver's List, no receiver-availability rule.
dataModelDeltas.impact: An anaesthetist-actor single-Booking move that creates the receiver's List in a free Slot (the Slot and List split makes this direct); the colleague finder (pushTargets) is reused for Bookings; optional notice (DM-41). The payable follows the Booking by derivation and a prepaid one sits in the AA Holding account (DM-21).
dataModelDeltas.verify_note: editRefusal confirms an anaesthetist cannot edit another's List; the whole-List move exists and the single-Booking path does not.

dataModelDeltas.title: The shared notification pool gains an active or resolved state with who and when, and a second source: an anaesthetist's 'ask the office to check'
dataModelDeltas.catalogue_says: One pool for the admin team, separate from the to-do list, shown as a dashboard panel with active notices newest first and a count. A notice is active or resolved only: any admin resolves it by ticking, which hides it for all (who and when kept; 'show resolved' brings it back); never expires; no per-user read state. Sources: an anaesthetist moving a List (US-13.8.2) and an alert on a List or Booking with a note from an anaesthetist who is unsure ('ask the office to check', US-03.6.3; opening it goes to that List or Booking). A single-Booking move may notify optionally.

dataModelDeltas.verify_note: notifications.ts header confirms append-only, no read or actioned state, postNotification the only writer.

dataModelDeltas.title: The anaesthetist profile holds mandatory bank account details and a mandatory HPI CPN (the rest of the master data is built)
dataModelDeltas.catalogue_says: Profile holds contact details, registration number, HPI CPN, bank account details held in the system (not Xero only) and the dollar value per unit (the unit rate), the only billing setting; no GST period, no prepaid setting. Bank details are mandatory (Greg, 28 Oct) and so is the HPI CPN ('where available' removed, Donald, 29 Oct): a record saved without either is refused. Surgeons' rooms, surgeon profile, groups and hospital contact email are master data.
dataModelDeltas.prototype_has: Surgeon rooms, profile, groups and hospital contact email built in Phase 17. Anaesthetist (types.ts:209) holds contact, unit value, hpiId (a blank is accepted, types.ts:216 to :222), start date, active; no bank details; still carries gstPeriod (DM-29).
dataModelDeltas.impact: Bank account fields on Anaesthetist, a required-field guard on HPI CPN and bank details in the Master Data form and store action, and seed values; used by the payables run (DM-25; OQ-111). Low risk, any time.
dataModelDeltas.verify_note: Anaesthetist type read: hpiId documented as blank-allowed and no bank field.

dataModelDeltas.title: Hospital bookings land on a matching screen as import rows with an admin decision; unmatched rows and rows with no NHI wait in a queue
dataModelDeltas.catalogue_says: The first release takes hospital bookings however each hospital provides them onto a review-and-merge screen. For each row the admin matches it to a List and Booking, creates a Booking on an existing List, creates a List in an anaesthetist's Slot or a Draft List, or rejects it; later updates to a matched Booking show field differences for approval; each row shows its procedure text as received. Unmatched rows and rows with no NHI stay in the unmatched queue; nothing is applied silently. Automatic schedule and sync removed (US-02.1.5); removal detection, surgeon PDF ingest and automatic matching are Future Work.

'hospitalRow' is reserved as a Draft List origin (types.ts:567) and the draftListActions parameter, but nothing emits it. No import row, match decision, difference view or unmatched queue.

dataModelDeltas.verify_note: hospitalRow confirmed reserved but never emitted; US-02.2.1, US-02.2.3 and US-14.6.2 confirmed in the Future Work lane so only the matching screen is in scope.

dataModelDeltas.title: A stub stands in a List for an incoming booking that could not be posted, held on an identifier other than the NHI
dataModelDeltas.catalogue_says: When an incoming booking cannot become a Booking (for example no NHI), a stub shows in its place on its List and the other Bookings are added as usual. It is held on an identifier other than the NHI, so probably a separate record on the List, not a Booking (the NHI rule still holds for Bookings). Anaesthetists and the office see it clearly marked as a booking with a problem; the office resolves it from the unmatched queue and the Booking then takes the stub's place (our reading). Feature is Open: it sits against the 19 Oct ruling (OQ-49) that such a booking waits at intake only, and waits on OQ-118 for Vanessa and Ben (whether the anaesthetist sees a stub at all).

dataModelDeltas.impact: A Stub record on the List (id, List, source-row reference, reason, text as received) outside the Bookings table, drawn in both anaesthetists' apps and the Admin List view with a problem mark and replaced by the Booking on resolution. Needs DM-30 and takes rows from DM-34's queue (before DM-34, processMessage can create it). Confirm OQ-118 first: if the answer is 'no stub' this delta closes. Seed one demo stub; PERSIST_VERSION bump.

dataModelDeltas.title: Explicit-save change sets, an on-demand update email draft picked from the change history, and email templates
dataModelDeltas.catalogue_says: An admin saves Booking edits explicitly (unsaved-changes warning); each save records fields changed (before, after, who, when) in the append-only history. A Booking admin screen has an on-demand 'draft update email' button: the admin picks changes and a mailto compose window opens prefilled (hospital contact for a cover change, surgeon's room for a Booking change), about 2,000 characters, nothing sent or recorded. Templates are user-configurable per kind of change. Automatic sending is Future.
dataModelDeltas.prototype_has: Append-only audit per mutation (AuditEntry types.ts:1095, mutate.ts), not grouped into save sets; edits apply immediately (editBooking, lifecycle.ts:416); no email draft, no templates. Contact emails it needs exist (Phase 17).
dataModelDeltas.impact: A change-set grouping on audit entries (or a draft buffer), an email-draft launcher and a template master; the admin edit form becomes explicit-save. Launched from DM-41 notices.
dataModelDeltas.verify_note: US-02.3.5 (automatic sending) confirmed in the Future Work lane and excluded; the rest in scope.

dataModelDeltas.title: Reference data: a master public-holiday calendar, a repeatable one-off data load and maintenance screens for the new masters
dataModelDeltas.catalogue_says: Admins maintain all reference data in one place: hospitals with contact email, surgeons and groups, rooms, anaesthetists, Slot statuses, recurring bookings, master and per-hospital holiday calendars, RVG groups, modifiers, contract holders (insurers among them: no separate insurer list) and Contracts with lines. Loaded once by a developer-run, repeatable data load, then edited by hand with every change recorded. Contract schedule upload is Future Work (US-04.2.13).
dataModelDeltas.prototype_has: Master Data has CRUD for hospitals, anaesthetists, surgeons, rooms, statuses, recurring bookings, holidays and Contracts. The RVG code and Modifier code views are view-only tables with no store action to add, edit or retire (ReferenceViews.tsx:234, :255). Holidays are per hospital only (types.ts:1000), no master calendar; seeds are TypeScript fixtures; no data-load script.
dataModelDeltas.impact: CRUD for the new masters (DM-13, DM-48, DM-07/09, DM-44) and write paths for the existing RVG and modifier masters, a master holiday calendar feeding each hospital's, and optionally a repeatable load script. The Insurer maintenance screen goes with DM-48. Mostly follows the entity deltas.
dataModelDeltas.verify_note: Upheld; added that the RVG and modifier masters are view-only in the prototype, so they need write paths as well as new fields.

dataModelDeltas.title: Warning routine: the model and the dashboard to-do list are built; the remaining rules land as their source entities do
dataModelDeltas.catalogue_says: One routine raises warnings (several per Booking, before- or after-procedure, mild or strong) that never block: unpaid prepayment, billable patient with a balance, child as payer, base units outside the RVG range, insurer-will-pay with no insurer Contract (review), and now an insured Booking with no approval number (where it shows is OQ-93). They show on the admin to-do list where an admin clears them and as a triangle on the Booking in both apps. The patient balance alert also shows the anaesthetist as a colour code on the Booking in their List. Settings and switching checks off are Future.
dataModelDeltas.prototype_has: Built in Phases 15a and 15a2: Warning, WarningRule, WarningClearance and AppSettings, one registered rule 'prepaymentUnpaid' (WarningRuleId, domain/warnings/types.ts:20), a stored office clearance, derived open warnings read by the admin to-do list (AdminApp.tsx:225) and a Booking flag in both apps.
dataModelDeltas.impact: Only rules remain, each widening WarningRuleId as its source lands: child payer (DM-11), insurer-will-pay with no insurer Contract and missing approval number (DM-12), out-of-range units (DM-43), billable patient with a balance (DM-23). The dashboard tick also resolves notices (DM-41). A Contract changed by the anaesthetist is an audit and review flag (DM-10), not a warning.
dataModelDeltas.verify_note: One rule type and one rule file confirmed; US-13.7.4 (settings) confirmed in the Future Work lane.

dataModelDeltas.title: Prepayment: started by picking a prepaid Contract, amount is the line's price, invoice generated when an admin approves it (an optional step), prepaid Procedures left off the final invoice with nothing deducted
dataModelDeltas.catalogue_says: Picking a prepaid-flagged Contract starts the prepayment, detected per Procedure and re-checked when Procedures, Contract or payer change (not on a move). The payer is normally a person but a holder-billing Contract is not forbidden from being prepaid (OQ-73 revised). The amount is the full price on the line, which must be above zero, shown to the anaesthetist; never a deposit or estimate; the Contract is never editable by the anaesthetist (OQ-96). The invoice is generated when an admin approves it, an optional step AA can switch off, then sent with a standard letter; its pair is a receivable from the payer and a payable to the AA Holding account (DM-21). A prepaid Procedure keeps its invoiced price if the Contract changes (OQ-104, confirmed by Ben). Afterwards BTM is reference only: no automatic invoice or credit, extra or lesser work by hand. The final invoice leaves every prepaid Procedure off and deducts nothing (OQ-116, 29 Oct): mixed Bookings invoice only the not-prepaid ones, all-prepaid has no final invoice, and multi-procedure ranking still counts all Procedures. Open: Contract changed after the prepayment is sent or paid (US-06.3.7, OQ-119), naming the anaesthetist (OQ-120), release trigger (OQ-125). FT-06.4 is Retired (moved to FT-06.5).
dataModelDeltas.prototype_has: Prepayment is Procedure.patientPaymentCategory 'selfFundedPrepayment' plus prepaymentDetail full or split (types.ts:794,:804,:846,:848), derived on the Billable Party route only (selectors.ts:574). The office raises the invoice by hand (prepaymentActions.ts:52) with no approval step or setting; a split deposit is a flat figure with the balance billed at the run and a visible deduction line (invoiceBuild.ts:380, :296 to :460); a full prepayment invoices an estimated fee from feeFor, not a Contract price. Unpaid warning built (prepaymentUnpaid.ts), aligned.
dataModelDeltas.impact: Remove PrepaymentDetail, the split path, the payment category and the netting deduction line entirely (OQ-116 answered: it no longer survives even for mixed Bookings); the run skips prepaid Procedures but still ranks all; trigger and amount read the prepaid Contract's line (needs DM-07 flags and price guard, DM-09, DM-11); Invoice gains a 'held for approval' state under a switchable setting (default on) and a letter-template master. OQ-119 and OQ-120 stay open. Before DM-21.
dataModelDeltas.verify_note: FT-06.4 confirmed Retired; the deduction line text 'Less pre-payment deposit already invoiced' read at invoiceBuild.ts:380; approval step text read in US-06.3.1 and US-08.4.1.

dataModelDeltas.title: AA Holding account: the prepayment's payable is a creditor in the payables sub-ledger, and a journal transfer moves it to the anaesthetist who did the List at authorisation
dataModelDeltas.catalogue_says: A prepayment is not paid to the anaesthetist: its pair's other side is the AA Holding account (formerly prepay holding account), a creditor in the payables sub-ledger beside each anaesthetist ('a fake anaesthetist'), not a bank account and not a Xero ledger account; its balance is all prepayments for procedures not yet done; the money sits in AA's trust account (the bank account). It is never paid itself and only the system pays out of it. Two steps: collected against the account, then at List authorisation a journal transfer (an accounting move, not a payment) moves it to the anaesthetist who did the List, who is paid in the normal run. Cancelling a prepaid Booking automatically credits the invoice if unpaid or refunds in full by the system if paid (OQ-115 answered); a replacement Booking starts its own prepayment; a move changes nothing. Open: release trigger (OQ-125), Contract changed after payment (OQ-119).
dataModelDeltas.prototype_has: No holding account. Soft cancel keeps the Booking and charges no fee (cancelBooking, lifecycle.ts:362) but credits and refunds nothing. The prepayment's ACCPAY is to the anaesthetist and released pro rata as money arrives (payableRelease.ts:16; paymentActions.ts:69), so the anaesthetist can be paid before the procedure.
dataModelDeltas.impact: A ledger creditor record for the AA Holding account as payee; the release rule holds the prepayment payable until authorisation then writes the transfer pair to the List's anaesthetist (a move needs no payee change); cancelling a prepaid Booking triggers an automatic credit or refund (needs DM-24); only system actions may pay out of it; draft Xero pair to a holding-account contact; balance shown in DM-23. Needs DM-20 and DM-22.
dataModelDeltas.verify_note: payableReleasedFor confirmed to release pro rata to the amount received with no hold; cancelBooking touches no money.

dataModelDeltas.title: Events on a Procedure (pre-op, post-op, billing event, additional invoice, credit, refund) replace the post-op addendum Booking and the other billing lines
dataModelDeltas.catalogue_says: An event is anything recorded against a Procedure after set-up: its own element listed on the Procedure in both apps. Pre-op and post-op events carry their own date and time, record a time or fixed fee, take no other modifiers, have an 'invoice' tick and a 'same as the Procedure's billable party' tick (the default). A billing event is a free-form charge or credit; other billing lines are merged into events; a refund can show as one. Events appear on no List or schedule, even dated another day: they live with the Booking (28 Oct). How and when an event is billed (a line on the Procedure's invoice or a separate invoice, now or next run) is reopened for Vanessa (OQ-121).
dataModelDeltas.prototype_has: A post-op addendum is a new linked Booking (bookingType 'postOpAddendum', addendumOfBookingId; types.ts:760) running its own capture, submit, authorise and bill cycle (bookingActions.ts:199). Late fee lines are BillingLines added before invoicing (billingLineActions.ts:46). No event record, invoice tick, billable-party tick or same-run versus next-run rule.
dataModelDeltas.impact: New Event entity (procedure, kind, date and time, time or fixed fee, invoiced flag, billable party or same-as, invoice link); replaces the addendum Booking (6 non-test files) and the post-invoice billing-line path; events are never a List or Slot entry; the run picks events up (rule parameterised until OQ-121); both apps list them. After DM-10 and DM-08; DM-18 and DM-24 are event kinds. DM-46's removal waits on this.
dataModelDeltas.verify_note: Addendum fields confirmed in types.ts and 6 non-test files re-grepped.

dataModelDeltas.title: Additional invoice: a free-form invoice recorded as an event, to any billable party, with its own ledger pair when raised after the original has gone
dataModelDeltas.catalogue_says: An admin (any Procedure) or the anaesthetist (their own) adds a free-form invoice (description, quantity, amount; no Contract or unit rules) against a Procedure to any billable party, traceable both ways to the original, recorded as an event, through the standard review step. Raised after the original invoice has gone, it has its own number, ledger pair, Xero pair and payable (before approval it is a line on that invoice). Uses: late post-op charges, extra or lesser work on prepaid or fixed-price work (by hand), splitting a combined Procedure.
dataModelDeltas.prototype_has: Invoice.kind 'standard' | 'prePayment' (types.ts:1120) with a bookingId and no link to an original invoice or Procedure; priced lines only (InvoiceLine.procedureId optional, :1131). No free-form entry and no second-invoice lineage.
dataModelDeltas.impact: Invoice.kind widens (additional, credit note) with originalInvoiceId and procedureId; free-form line entry UI in both apps; same pair creation and Xero handoff; an event added before approval joins the invoice. Needs DM-17 and DM-22.
dataModelDeltas.verify_note: Invoice and InvoiceLine read in types.ts; kind union confirmed.

dataModelDeltas.title: A wrong invoice is credited in full then rebilled; the payable is reversed by a negative invoice
dataModelDeltas.catalogue_says: An invoice is never edited or partly adjusted: it is credited in full and a new corrected invoice raised, each traceable to the original; the ledger payable and Xero pair are reversed and re-created together. The payable reversal is a negative invoice to the anaesthetist, netted in their next payment run and shown on the remittance advice. A credit note is not a refund. Rebill may start from a draft copy. Cancelling a prepaid Booking raises its credit (unpaid) or refund (paid) automatically (US-06.5.2). Credit and new invoices are events.
dataModelDeltas.prototype_has: Nothing: no credit note, negative payable or rebill; invoices immutable once raised; BillingPipelineStatus runs pending, invoiced, handedOff, partPaid, paid, disbursed, failed, with no credited or reversed state (types.ts:1137 to :1145).
dataModelDeltas.impact: CreditNote entity linked to its invoice, a negative payable record and Xero credit mirroring, a rebill-from-copy action, new BillingCase states; the prepaid-cancel path (DM-21) calls this credit. Needs DM-18 and DM-22; precedes DM-25's netting and DM-21's refund.
dataModelDeltas.verify_note: BillingPipelineStatus union read in types.ts; the validator comment 'a negative invoice is a credit note, which this system never raises' also confirms.

dataModelDeltas.title: The internal ledger holds both halves of each pair as its own records (including the holding-account payable), with the payable independent of Xero, structured as control accounts and sub-ledgers
dataModelDeltas.catalogue_says: For every invoice the engine creates a linked receivable from the billable party and a payable to the anaesthetist in its own ledger, the system of record, which Xero only mirrors (ACCREC and draft ACCPAY created together; a prepayment's payable is to the AA Holding account). The ledger tracks money in and out per patient and per anaesthetist and survives Xero contact archiving. The ledger is structured as control accounts (debtors, creditors) holding totals and sub-ledgers (patients; anaesthetists plus the AA Holding account) holding detail, each reconciled to its control account; the trust account is the bank account analysed by anaesthetist due. Payables carry the receivable's number with '-P'; each is a buyer-created tax invoice (new IRD name to confirm; how many, per procedure, payment or weekly run, is unsettled, OQ-29). Whether our system or Xero sends invoices is a build choice.
dataModelDeltas.prototype_has: The ledger is the billing slice (Invoice, InvoiceLine, BillingCase with receivedAmount, authorisedAmount, disbursedAmount and Xero ids; types.ts:1112 to :1182), called a mirror in code. The payable document exists only as XeroAccPay in the Xero simulation (types.ts:1244), so it has no ledger record of its own. '-P' number stored (:1250). No control accounts or sub-ledgers.
dataModelDeltas.impact: Promote the Payable into the ledger (id, number, amount, authorised, disbursed, status, payee: anaesthetist or AA Holding account) with Xero downstream; split BillingCase into receivable and payable sides; structure as control accounts with patient and creditors sub-ledgers reconciled to each other (DM-23 shows the imbalance); rewire payments, payables run, selectors and Xero view. Foundation for DM-21, DM-18, DM-24, DM-23, DM-25, DM-29.
dataModelDeltas.verify_note: Ledger-in-slice and the Xero-only payable document confirmed in types.ts.

dataModelDeltas.title: Derived ledger positions for the whole ledger, per anaesthetist and per patient; a flat outstanding list without ageing; patient balance alerts
dataModelDeltas.catalogue_says: The Admin App shows the ledger's position for the whole ledger (receivables outstanding, receipts held, payables due, disbursed, any imbalance, including each sub-ledger against its control account and the trust account analysed by anaesthetist due) and a single anaesthetist, plus a patient's outstanding invoices across anaesthetists. The anaesthetist's outstanding list is flat, oldest first, no ageing (US-12.2.1, OQ-59). Booking or matching a patient with a balance alerts staff: mild under the threshold (90 days, fixed until AA asks), strong above, mild for a credit balance, never a block; anaesthetists also see the alert on the Booking in their List as a colour code (28 Oct; clearing an alert is parked). Follow-up actions are recorded.
dataModelDeltas.prototype_has: A per-anaesthetist outstanding list built per ACCPAY invoice with agingDays and a bucket (selectors.ts:874 to :952; AccountsScreen), which the catalogue now excludes. A boolean patientHasOutstandingPriorEpisode check (selectors.ts:552) shown as 'Prior balance' only in the admin billing monitor (BillingMonitorScreen.tsx:210); no threshold, mild or strong, nothing on the anaesthetist's List. No whole-ledger, per-anaesthetist or per-patient balance screen; no follow-up record.
dataModelDeltas.impact: New pure selectors over the ledger and three admin views; remove ageing buckets from the web Accounts and dashboard; the threshold in appSettings; a FollowUpAction record; the mild or strong alert on the Booking row in both anaesthetist apps; a reconciliation view. Needs DM-22 and DM-11; the alert rule lands in DM-31.
dataModelDeltas.verify_note: US-12.2.1 read: flat list, no ageing buckets or chips; agingDays and bucket confirmed in selectors.ts:874 to :952.

dataModelDeltas.title: Weekly payment cycle with period approval of BCTIs and a remittance advice that nets negative invoices
dataModelDeltas.catalogue_says: A payable is released when its receivable is paid, for exactly the amount received. Payments run on a weekly cycle named by ISO week: Friday the ledger is closed and snapshotted, Monday for the office to clear problems, Tuesday the schedule of released payables goes to the accountant, anomalies roll into the next cycle. BCTIs for a period are approved before the run (who approves is open). The remittance advice shows invoices paid and negative invoices netted. Whether payment is made in Xero or from the new system is OQ-111.
dataModelDeltas.prototype_has: runPayables (payablesActions.ts:147) pays every authorised-minus-disbursed amount at once under a payablesRunId (Disbursement, types.ts:1361). No cycle or week identity, approval state, held-out anomalies, remittance advice or netting.
dataModelDeltas.impact: PaymentRun entity (ISO week, status, held-out items), an approval state on payables, a remittance document, netting of negative payables. Needs DM-24 and DM-22. Proposed in the catalogue, so keep it replaceable.
dataModelDeltas.verify_note: US-10.2.7 is Proposed (status 1), so the delta is conditional and flagged replaceable.

dataModelDeltas.title: The GST report lists the payments AA passed to the anaesthetist in the month; the anaesthetist's GST period goes
dataModelDeltas.catalogue_says: Each month each anaesthetist gets a list of the payments AA passed to them in the month with the GST component of each, for their GST return. It lists payments, not invoices sent; outstanding amounts fall into a later month; downloadable, so a web-app report. No GST period on the profile (US-12.1.2 Retired). All prices held ex GST (US-12.2.2, EP-12, US-12.1.1, US-05.2.7; OQ-29).
dataModelDeltas.prototype_has: BillingReceipt carries a GST component of amounts received into AA (types.ts:1192; gstComponentOf, paymentActions.ts:34); the web Accounts GST report reads those receipts. Anaesthetist.gstPeriod monthly|biMonthly|sixMonthly (types.ts:215,:237) is held and edited (10 non-test files).
dataModelDeltas.impact: Re-base the report on payments made to the anaesthetist (the payable's paid side from DM-22) grouped by calendar month; remove gstPeriod, its seed values and editor. Follows DM-22.
dataModelDeltas.verify_note: US-12.1.2 confirmed Retired; gstPeriod reader count (10) re-grepped.

dataModelDeltas.title: Audit covers invoices, credit notes, master data and Contract changes but not disbursements, payments or receipts
dataModelDeltas.catalogue_says: The audit trail shows who or what made each audited change: creates, updates, reassignments, authorisations, invoices, credit notes, master data and Contract and time-entry changes. Disbursements, payments and receipts are not audited there, since they are recorded in Xero; depth is for the developers (US-13.5.2, FT-13.5).
dataModelDeltas.prototype_has: Every mutation is audited through mutate(), including simulated Xero payments and disbursements (paymentActions.ts 'xero.paymentReceived' :186 and 'xero.accpayAuthorised' :193; payablesActions.ts 'xero.disbursed' :132).
dataModelDeltas.impact: Policy note, not a structural gap: the prototype audits a superset, so nothing must change; either keep audit uniform in the demo or filter payment and disbursement entries from the audit viewer. Credit notes (DM-24) and Contract versions (DM-07) must be audited.
dataModelDeltas.verify_note: Weakest delta: US-13.5.2 text confirms the exclusion but the prototype audits a superset and nothing is missing. Kept as a policy note because phase docs 36 and 39 already cite DM-45; could be dropped without model impact.

dataModelDeltas.title: A SUBMITTED List stays editable by the anaesthetist until AUTHORISED, and a List leaves the anaesthetist's main view at AUTHORISED
dataModelDeltas.catalogue_says: Once SUBMITTED the anaesthetist can still see the List and change its Bookings until the office authorises it; changes audited, office sees them at review, last change stands. Submitting only tells the office it has work and makes the List less prominent. The main view shows upcoming work, earlier Lists not yet authorised and submitted ones not yet authorised; an authorised List leaves the main view (not at submit, billing or payment), its invoices show as outstanding balances, and it stays findable by search (US-03.1.6). AUTHORISED stays immutable.
dataModelDeltas.prototype_has: editRefusal refuses an anaesthetist once a List is SUBMITTED ('listSubmitted', lifecycle.ts:50 to :75, reassignBooking :574). A List leaves the anaesthetist's forward views when the billing run stamps List.billedAtISO (isListBilled, selectors.ts:390; types.ts:641; ForwardListsScreen.tsx:76; DashboardScreen.tsx:88), not at AUTHORISED.
dataModelDeltas.impact: Relax the anaesthetist edit rule to ACTIVE and SUBMITTED (16 non-test files name 'SUBMITTED'), keep AUTHORISED locked, make anaesthetist edits to a SUBMITTED List visible at review; switch the forward-view filter from billedAtISO to AUTHORISED and keep search for older work. The billedAtISO stamp stays for the office monitor.
dataModelDeltas.verify_note: editRefusal and isListBilled read directly; the code comment itself cites the old 3rd-review rule that the catalogue replaced.

dataModelDeltas.title: An anaesthetist's unavailability is never a conflict: conflicts cover hospital closures only
dataModelDeltas.catalogue_says: A List conflicts only when its hospital is closed: a soft warning, never a block. An anaesthetist's unavailability, short-notice sickness included, is never a conflict flag: a List never stays with an unavailable anaesthetist, who returns it to the office or assigns it to a colleague there and then, choosing what the vacated Slot becomes. A recurring booking landing on an unavailable Slot becomes a Draft List.
dataModelDeltas.prototype_has: ListConflict kind 'availability' | 'holiday' (types.ts:446); conflicts.ts derives an availability conflict for a List in a closed-status Slot (:114). The anaesthetist's own path is guarded (Phase 32) but the office's sickness-record path keeps the List with the availability conflict (availabilityActions.ts:190 applySessionWrites; demoSimulations.ts:49 simulateSickness).
dataModelDeltas.impact: Remove the 'availability' conflict kind and derivation; the office recording sickness must also force a return or assign (or send the List to Draft Lists); Conflicts screen and dashboard shrink to holiday closures; tests and the sickness demo trigger rewritten. Independent of every other delta.
dataModelDeltas.verify_note: OQ-81 answer and US-01.5.2 and US-01.5.4 read: availability is never a conflict. The code comment still cites the superseded 'OQ-81 part 3' reading.

dataModelDeltas.title: Contract changes are staged, reviewed on a dashboard and submitted together as a new dated version
dataModelDeltas.catalogue_says: The office maintains one Contract at a time on a header and lines screen. Edits are staged and shown on a review dashboard; the office sets the effective date and submits together, all or nothing, creating the new dated version and recording what changed. The dashboard shows header before/after, counts of lines added, altered, removed and unchanged, each altered line's changed values (highlighting any that become blank), blocking errors (duplicate codes, missing or past effective date, a second future-dated version) and non-blocking warnings (affected Bookings). A one-line fix follows the same path. Upload in the AA template is Future Work.
dataModelDeltas.prototype_has: contractActions.ts edits a Contract and its price rows in place, immediately, with an audit entry (createContract :53, editContract :106, addContractPrice :200, editContractPrice :235). No staged change set, diff or effective-date step.
dataModelDeltas.impact: A staged ContractChange per Contract (header patch plus line adds, alters, removes) applied only on submit, a pure diff builder and the review dashboard screen; submit creates the version through DM-07 and runs the relink and affected-Booking list. After DM-07 and DM-09. Upload stays out.
dataModelDeltas.verify_note: US-04.1.6 is Proposed (status 1), not Future Work; US-04.2.13 upload confirmed in the Future Work lane and excluded.

dataModelDeltas.title: The completion gate is three conditions: a Contract, times where the Contract prices from time, and an explanation for each claimed modifier; the billing validator no longer decides completion
dataModelDeltas.catalogue_says: Before the anaesthetist can mark a Booking complete, every Procedure on it must have a Contract, its times recorded where the Contract prices from time (not on a fixed price), and a short explanation for any modifier claimed (US-03.6.1). The RVG code is optional; the holder's references and the insurance approval number are the office's job, and a missing approval number is a warning, not a block (US-11.4.3). A Procedure the anaesthetist cannot complete is sent to the office (US-03.6.3). Submission is rejected when no price can be worked out (domain model section 3). Incomplete Bookings are listed (US-03.6.2).
dataModelDeltas.prototype_has: completionBlockersFor (lifecycle.ts:101) delegates the whole gate to validateBookingForBilling (validateBookingForBilling.ts:104), the same pre-flight the billing run uses, so completion is blocked by about a dozen billing-setup checks: an explicit billing route, an RVG code or a billing line, both times on any RVG-coded Procedure, an in-range selected base value, insurer accepting direct claims, a patient payment category and prepayment detail, the Method 3 gate, a price-override reason and non-negative total, line conservation and the hospital reference (:125 to :290). No modifier explanation check and no 'times only where the Contract prices from time' test.
dataModelDeltas.impact: Replace the validator's route, insurer, category, prepayment, Method 3, override-reason and conservation branches (each already named as removed in DM-10, DM-20, DM-46, DM-14 and DM-28) with the three-condition completion rule, and split completion (the anaesthetist's rule, completionBlockersFor) from billing pre-flight (the engine's 'no price can be worked out' rejection, DM-50). Out-of-range units and a missing approval number move to warnings (DM-31, DM-12). The mobile submit sheet and BookingDetailBody read the same failures; the validator's Vitest suite is rewritten. Needs DM-10, DM-44 and DM-13 (optional RVG code); done with DM-46 so the validator is rewritten once.
dataModelDeltas.verify_note: Added by the verifier: the catalogue's completion rule is three conditions, while the prototype makes the whole billing validator the completion gate (lifecycle.ts:101 to :118). The branches are removed piecemeal in other deltas but the rewrite of the gate itself and the split of completion from billing pre-flight had no owner.

deltaSummary: Verified all 40 draft deltas against the catalogue and the code; none was refuted and none dropped. I kept DM-45 as upheld, flagging it as the weakest: it is a policy note (the prototype audits a superset), and the phase docs already cite it. I corrected 8 and added 1, so the list is now 41 deltas (kept ids unchanged). Corrected: DM-13 (34 seed rows, not 33; RVG Master Data view is read-only so the master has no write path), DM-38 (same finding for RVG and modifier views), DM-10 (the prototype already stores governingContractId on the Procedure and uses it while in effect, so the gap is versioning, lock, anaesthetist change right and route removal, not resolution from scratch), DM-43 (captured-units override is the nearest existing seam), DM-44 (17 readers not 13; no DOB age modifier in billing code), DM-46 (26 files not 25), DM-49 (mastersActions refs :87 and :182), DM-48 (note on existing SurgeonGroup and organisations masters, kept upheld). Scope check: FT-06.4, FT-11.4, US-11.4.1, US-11.4.2, FT-04.4, US-04.4.x, US-05.1.6, US-04.2.12, US-03.5.3, US-03.3.6, US-03.3.7, US-04.2.5, US-05.3.4, US-04.2.7, US-12.1.2 confirmed Retired; the 19 Future Work lane stories (US-02.2.1, 02.2.3, 02.5.1 to 02.5.4, 02.5.6, 02.3.5, 02.4.4, 04.2.13, 04.3.6, 04.3.7, 13.7.4, 14.x) are cited only as boundaries. Added DM-59 (RuleChange, M): the catalogue's completion gate is three conditions (Contract, times where the Contract prices from time, explanation per claimed modifier; US-03.6.1), but the prototype uses the whole billing validator as the completion gate (lifecycle.ts:101), so the validator rewrite and the split of completion from billing pre-flight had no owner. Added Procedure.accRelated and Int Notes/Op Notes to the prototype-only list. The file domain-model-delta.md at /Users/d.fraser/Development/Stratos Dev/AnaesthesiaAssociatesRFP/docs/prototype-build/catch-up/analysis/ now matches: 41 deltas, header and counts updated (RuleChange 8, M 20), a second-verification paragraph, a DM-59 index row and section, and the suggested order notes DM-59.

reverseFindings.title: Attachments on Bookings and Lists are fully built
reverseFindings.explanation: US-03.1.3 was Retired 16 October (no requirement; Ben does not want the rooms' PDFs on a Booking). The prototype still lets the anaesthetist attach files to any Booking and List on mobile and web, the office sees them in the session drawer, a theatre-list PDF is seeded and S1 touches it.
reverseFindings.verify_note: US-03.1.3 status 6 with a real withdrawal note (Greg: comfortable removing it). Attachments section and List attachments panel confirmed at the cited lines; seeded AT0001 confirmed.

reverseFindings.title: GST period is a per-anaesthetist setting and a selector on the report
reverseFindings.explanation: US-12.1.2 is Retired (no GST period on the profile; GST report is monthly). The prototype stores gstPeriod on every anaesthetist, asks for it when adding or editing one, seeds Dr Whitaker six-monthly, and the web GST report has a Monthly / Bi-monthly / Six-monthly switch.
reverseFindings.verify_note: US-12.1.2 status 6 ('no GST period on the profile', Greg: 'way too complicated'); US-12.2.2 says monthly. Code confirmed incl. cast.ts sixMonthly for Whitaker and AnaesthetistRecord display.

reverseFindings.title: Rate x time billing line and the Method 3 individual-arrangement gate
reverseFindings.explanation: US-03.3.7 retired into US-03.3.6, itself Retired (other billing lines merge into Events; a fixed-rate Contract needs no billing line, OQ-89). The prototype still offers an hours x hourly rate line gated by a permits-individual-arrangement Contract flag, with a seeded hourly Contract and rate x time Bookings. Fixed-amount ancillary lines also remain and can stay until Events are built.
reverseFindings.verify_note: US-03.3.6 notes say the unit x rate line 'is removed' (OQ-89) and its examples moved to Events. Gate, seeded Aria hourly Contract, rateTimeBooking seed markers and the Contract edit switch all confirmed.

reverseFindings.title: Anaesthetist price adjustment: reason mandatory, offered on every Contract including prepaid and fixed prices, no per-Contract flag
reverseFindings.explanation: US-03.5.3 (reason) is Retired into US-03.5.1: no reason needed, and a per-Contract flag decides what the anaesthetist can change. 28 October added: never on a prepaid Contract (OQ-96) and never on a fixed price (OQ-117). The prototype demands a reason, offers override on every Contract, and has no flag.
reverseFindings.verify_note: US-03.5.1 text and ACs read directly: 'No reason is needed', fixed price never open to override, prepaid not editable. Code: reason mandatory in OverrideCard, PriceOverrideSheet ('Reason (required)') and the validator; no per-Contract editable flag exists.

reverseFindings.title: Prepayment is a per-Booking payment category with split deposit or estimated full fee, netted from the final invoice, no settlement on cancel
reverseFindings.explanation: Live model: per-Procedure trigger by a prepaid Contract (US-06.2.1), fixed price above zero, not editable by the anaesthetist, optional admin approval, prepaid Procedure left off the final invoice with nothing deducted (OQ-116), automatic credit or refund on cancel (OQ-115). The prototype uses a payment category, full or split deposit, a BTM estimate, deducts the deposit as a negative line, bills the balance, and cancelling settles nothing (a cancelled Booking just raises no prepayment invoice).
reverseFindings.verify_note: US-06.4.1, US-06.2.1, OQ-115, OQ-116 and OQ-96 read directly and say exactly this. Trigger (billableParty + selfFundedPrepayment), PrepaymentDetail full/split, 'Less pre-payment deposit already invoiced' line and cancel handling all confirmed.

reverseFindings.title: Protected default Type 1 Contract per hospital and direct-claim insurer, auto-created and used as a fallback
reverseFindings.explanation: FT-04.4 and US-04.4.1 (Retired) mandated a default Contract per hospital and insurer; US-04.3.3 replaces them: no hospital, insurer or procedure defaults, the one default is No contract (RVG), held by AA. The prototype mints a protected Type 1 default with each hospital and direct-claim insurer, forbids deleting or end-dating it, and falls back to it when a Procedure has no valid Contract.
reverseFindings.verify_note: US-04.3.3 says 'There are no hospital, insurer or procedure default Contracts, and nothing is derived from the List's location.' Code confirmed (isDefault true on create, DEFAULT_PROTECTED_MESSAGE, defaultContractFor fallback).

reverseFindings.title: Second-procedure pricing keyed on the procedure ordinal
reverseFindings.explanation: US-04.2.5 and US-05.3.4 are Retired (5 October, Donald): Contracts do not define second-procedure pricing; the RVG default applies (OQ-90). The prototype lets an admin key a Type 3 price row to a procedure ordinal, prices an add-on from it only when the row has an ordinal, and seeds a $950 second-procedure price.
reverseFindings.verify_note: Both retire notes state a real withdrawal, not a merge of the behaviour. Code confirmed (CP-BAR-3 ordinal 2 at $950, ordinal specificity match, fee.ts add-on exception).

reverseFindings.title: Additional procedures carry no modifier share; the above-four split is missing
reverseFindings.explanation: US-05.3.3 retired into US-05.3.1 (confirmed 19 October): modifier units on the primary while four or fewer, then split equally with remainder to the primary. The prototype gives an additional procedure time units only, locks B and M, and has no split.
reverseFindings.verify_note: US-05.3.1 AC 'Modifier split' read directly. Strictly the retirement is a merge, so the code implements the old RFP split-billing rule (a superseded decision) rather than a withdrawn feature; kind left as filed because the remedy is the same.

reverseFindings.title: P1 absorbed by the wrong codes, and struck through instead of shown selected at 0 units
reverseFindings.explanation: US-05.2.3 is Retired but US-05.1.4 and US-03.3.4 restore it correctly: P1 is included in the six Neurosurgery and fourteen Spine codes, shown selected at 0 units, nothing locked. The prototype marks demo codes (hip x3 and shoulder x2 are not in the RVG list) and shows an inert struck-through chip with a refusal caption.
reverseFindings.verify_note: Seed lines confirmed (hip, shoulder, lumbar absorb P1). Catalogue wording splits: US-05.1.4 says not locked, US-03.3.4's first paragraph says cannot be unselected; build to US-05.1.4 and the 20 October decision.

reverseFindings.title: Ranged base code is hard-bounded to the published range
reverseFindings.explanation: US-03.3.2 retired into US-03.3.1: the anaesthetist is shown the range (OQ-101 answered 29 October) and may enter any value; out-of-range warns the office, never blocks (OQ-56). The prototype already shows the range but clamps the stepper to it and refuses completion outside it.
reverseFindings.verify_note: US-03.3.1 text and 'Out of range' AC read directly; RangeUnitsRow clamps with Math.max/min and the validator fails an out-of-range baseUnitsSelected.

reverseFindings.title: The engine re-resolves Contract and payer at billing time; nothing is locked at AUTHORISED
reverseFindings.explanation: US-08.1.2 (Retired into US-08.1.1): the engine resolves no route or payer; it reads the Contract locked to each Procedure, snapshotted at AUTHORISED (US-04.3.5). The prototype falls back to the holder's default or resolves by route, derives the payer, snapshots no Contract, and Resolve and retry changes what a re-run prices.
reverseFindings.verify_note: US-08.1.1 and US-04.3.5 read directly. No Contract snapshot exists in code (only fee and rate snapshots); resolveContractForProcedure falls back by route and holder.

reverseFindings.title: Insurer master with an accepts-direct-claims flag, an Insurer route gated on it, and delivery hard-wired by insurer
reverseFindings.explanation: Retired 28 October (Donald: 'We don't have a master insurance list'): no insurer master, no direct-claims flag; an insurer is a contract holder, delivery is a holder setting (OQ-114), insurer and approval number are Booking fields with a missing number a warning. The prototype has the master and flag, an Insurers admin tab that mints a default Contract, a gated Insurer route, and upload-portal delivery by insurer kind.
reverseFindings.verify_note: FT-11.4 and US-11.4.1 notes read directly (insurers are 'just an instance of contract holders'; invoice output flag lives on the holder, US-04.1.5). All five code sites confirmed, incl. the 'Turn on' flip that creates a default Contract.

reverseFindings.title: Surgeon PDF upload and ingest is shown unbadged as product
reverseFindings.explanation: US-02.2.1 is in the Future Work swimlane. The Integrations Surgeon PDFs tab carries no Future badge while Messages and Feed config do: a facsimile beside editable rows, NHI correction and Ingest all, an Ingest PDF row demo action, and seeded surgeonPdf Bookings. OQ-108 is still unsettled after 27 October.
reverseFindings.verify_note: Swimlane 'Future Work' confirmed in US-02.2.1 frontmatter. TabButton for pdfs has no future prop; the ingest-pdf-row demo trigger has no badge.

reverseFindings.title: Automated modify, reschedule and cancel from hospital messages shown working, with a day move applied as a cross-List move
reverseFindings.explanation: All Future Work swimlane. Canned S13 to S15 messages apply with no admin: a cross-List move contradicts US-02.5.2 (a Booking on another day is cancel plus new), submitted Lists refuse inbound changes against US-02.5.4 (accepted until AUTHORISED), and a cancel of a prepaid Booking settles nothing (US-02.5.3, 28 October). Demo actions are already badged; keep S13 to S15 out of the script.
reverseFindings.verify_note: reassignBooking on S13 and the integration refusal when list.state is not ACTIVE confirmed in code; US-02.5.2 and US-02.5.4 titles and swimlanes confirmed.

reverseFindings.title: HL7 v2 to FHIR simulator, live drip, and Scenario S1 built on them
reverseFindings.explanation: HL7, FHIR and near-real-time are Future; the in-scope release is the St George's and Southern Cross download into a manual matching screen. Phase 14 badged the simulator and tabs and S1 now calls its beat an illustration, but the Integrations page intro, live-feed button and raw HL7 panes remain unbadged, and S1 still opens on a pushed message creating a Booking. Rework S1 around the matching screen when it exists.
reverseFindings.verify_note: Page intro text and live drip effect confirmed; S1 blurb already carries a Future caveat, so the residue is smaller than the original wording implied.

reverseFindings.title: Reliability tooling (retries, dead-letter queue, manual intervention): residual unbadged nav badge, patient names in the log
reverseFindings.explanation: FT-14.5 and US-14.5.1 are Future. The prototype retries three times, dead-letters, shows an unbadged amber attention badge on the side nav, offers Reprocess, and lists patient names in the message log where US-14.5.1 wants a restricted view. The Messages tab itself is already badged Future. Low priority.
reverseFindings.verify_note: Low-priority residue only: the nav badge (integrationBadge) and Patient column confirmed; the tab that hosts them is already badged Future.

reverseFindings.title: Further hospital feeds and automatic application with no matching step
reverseFindings.explanation: Further feeds and automatic matching are Future; the first release keeps a manual matching review with an unmatched queue for rows with no NHI. The prototype has three feeds including Christchurch Public and creates the Booking straight onto the List with no review, last-synced display or unmatched queue. The in-scope matching screen does not exist (code comments say 'Interim until Phase 33').
reverseFindings.verify_note: FEED-STG, FEED-CPH, FEED-SX confirmed; applyEffect S12 creates the Booking directly. The missing matching screen is a gap item (Phase 33) as well as a showcase problem.

reverseFindings.title: Billing route plus Type 1/2/3 Contracts, instead of one Contract per Procedure
reverseFindings.explanation: Supersedes Phase 08 route resolution and the 22 July billing-route rulings. Each Procedure selects one Contract that sets price and who is billed; behaviour is set by flags, not kinds; holders are hospitals, insurers, surgeons by practitioner ID and anaesthetists. The prototype uses a billing route, Type 1/2/3 Contracts picked by the office, and a payment category. Keep labelled until Phases 18 to 21.
reverseFindings.verify_note: US-04.3.3, US-04.1.5, US-08.1.1 and US-11.2.1 read directly and are consistent with this. Route is required by the validator at line 125.

reverseFindings.title: The anaesthetist's edit rights end at SUBMITTED
reverseFindings.explanation: Supersedes binding convention 6. Reversed 16 October and confirmed 19 October: the anaesthetist can edit a submitted List until the office AUTHORISES it. The prototype refuses any anaesthetist write once SUBMITTED ('Only the office can change it now'), hides edit controls, and the submit confirm tells her she cannot change the Bookings.
reverseFindings.verify_note: US-07.2.1 status 4 and its ACs ('submitted List... the change saves') read directly; refusal text and submit copy confirmed in code.

reverseFindings.title: A patient without an NHI is allowed (provisional record, NHI pending)
reverseFindings.explanation: The NHI is mandatory: no patient record without one; an incoming row without one waits at intake. On 28 October Greg proposed a stub on the List (FT-02.6, OQ-118 open); the 19 October rule stands until answered. The prototype takes NHI as optional, creates a provisional patient, shows NHI pending and seeds a no-NHI patient. Do not extend that path.
reverseFindings.verify_note: US-11.1.4 ACs read directly ('cannot be saved' without NHI; no Booking or patient record from an incoming row). FT-02.6 is status 2 (Open), so the stub idea is correctly left unresolved.

reverseFindings.title: Completion rules follow the RFP route and times, not the Contract, with no modifier explanation
reverseFindings.explanation: Supersedes the Phase 04 completion ruling. A Procedure completes with a Contract, its times (only where the Contract prices from time) and a short explanation per modifier; the RVG code is optional. The prototype requires a billing route, an RVG code or billing line, times whenever an RVG code is set, and asks for no modifier explanation.
reverseFindings.verify_note: US-03.6.1 (status 3) read directly; validator lines confirmed.

reverseFindings.title: ASA class auto-seeds modifier units
reverseFindings.explanation: Supersedes the 22 July ASA seeding values. US-03.3.4 pre-applies only the age modifier and base-included modifiers ('No other modifier is selected for the anaesthetist, whatever the patient's ASA grade'); ASA is chosen like any modifier with an explanation. Ben (27 October) accepted pre-selected zero-value positioning modifiers and did not name ASA (OQ-95 part 1 open). The prototype auto-adds the AS code from an ASA control. Moderate confidence; labelled simplification.
reverseFindings.verify_note: US-03.3.4 AC 'Nothing else pre-filled' and US-05.1.5 text confirm the direction; only OQ-95 part 1 (ASA) is formally open. Code confirmed (asaClass pushed into selected modifiers, ASA_SEED_UNITS).

reverseFindings.title: Post-op addendum is a new linked Booking on today's free session
reverseFindings.explanation: Supersedes the Phase 09 reading. A pre-op or post-op event is an element on the original Procedure, and since 28 October appears on no List or schedule; how it is billed is reopened (OQ-121, US-03.7.2 back to Verify). The prototype creates a second linked Booking on a List on today's free session running a full capture, submit and authorise cycle. The code itself marks this INTERIM until Phase 38b.
reverseFindings.verify_note: US-03.7.1 'Not on a List' AC and notes read directly; addPostOpAddendum creates a List and Booking.

reverseFindings.title: A prepaid invoice gets a full receivable and payable pair that pays the anaesthetist; the catalogue pays it into the AA Holding account
reverseFindings.explanation: Supersedes decision D-pre-invoice-pair. A prepayment is credited to the AA Holding account (a payables creditor, not a bank or Xero ledger account), approval is an optional step, release is a journal transfer made only by the system (trigger open, OQ-125), and cancel credits or refunds automatically. The prototype pays the anaesthetist through an ordinary pair, with no approval, holding account, transfer or cancel settlement.
reverseFindings.verify_note: xeroHandoff comment cites D-pre-invoice-pair verbatim; US-06.4.1 and OQ-115 say the payment is a transfer from the holding account, not a new invoice.

reverseFindings.title: Unavailability still produces a conflict flag, and the office path keeps the List
reverseFindings.explanation: Supersedes Phases 30 and 31. Since 19 October an anaesthetist never keeps a List on an unavailable Slot (planned or sickness): the transfer or return is forced and conflicts cover hospital closures only. The prototype still raises an Anaesthetist unavailable conflict, Simulate sickness leaves the List on the closed Slot, and the office can assign onto a closed session.
reverseFindings.verify_note: OQ-81 answer read directly ('never a conflict with the Bookings left in place'); expectedConflicts still emits kind 'availability' and simulateSickness only sets the Slot status.

reverseFindings.title: Provisional readings answered on 19 October are still built as provisional
reverseFindings.explanation: Supersedes the Phase 32 OQ-84 and notification-pool readings. OQ-84 is answered (whoever moves a List is asked whether the vacated Slot is Free or Unavailable), so only the 'still being confirmed' label is stale. OQ-79 is answered: notices are active or resolved, cleared by a tick, never expire; the prototype keeps every notice with no resolve state.
reverseFindings.verify_note: OQ-84, OQ-79 status 4 confirmed; US-01.4.1 and US-01.4.3 state the one path for everyone. Provisional captions confirmed in code.

reverseFindings.title: The office moves a single Booking to any List on any day (lower confidence)
reverseFindings.explanation: A List never moves day (OQ-87); a single Booking moves only to a colleague free in that Slot as a new List, never into an existing List (OQ-85). The prototype's office Move booking flow lets the office pick any day and any existing List, and it has no anaesthetist-side single-Booking move at all (a gap). The catalogue states the rule for the anaesthetist's own move only, so the office half is an owner question, not a defect.
reverseFindings.verify_note: US-01.4.7 opens 'In their app, an anaesthetist can move a single Booking' and OQ-85 answers the same; nothing forbids the office doing otherwise. Action changed from Rework to Keep as demo scaffold (raise with the owner); the only single-Booking move in the prototype is this office flow (grep of reassignBooking callers).

reverseFindings.title: Office edits to a Booking write through on every tap, with no Save
reverseFindings.explanation: Supersedes the 23 July write-through-per-tap ruling for the office. An admin edit applies only on an explicit Save, warns on leaving with unsaved edits and records changed fields for the update email. The Admin Booking detail wraps the same shared body, so there is no Save, Discard or unsaved warning.
reverseFindings.verify_note: US-02.3.2 ACs ('Explicit save', 'Unsaved warning') read directly; no Save, Discard or unsaved text in AdminBookingDetail.tsx.

reverseFindings.title: The anaesthetist's Booking shows no calculation, units or price
reverseFindings.explanation: Supersedes the 28 September owner decision that the Card shows no calculation. US-03.1.2 has the anaesthetist see the Contract's pricing basis with the figure, and US-03.5.1 lets them change it where the Contract allows. Confirm with Donald before changing; the web List table already shows units and fee while the Booking hides them. Lower confidence (his own decision).
reverseFindings.verify_note: US-03.1.2 (status 4) says 'its pricing basis with the figure'; showBookingTotal is false for anaesthetists. Kept as lower confidence because the earlier ruling was Donald's.

reverseFindings.title: The payer is a per-Procedure billable-party record tied to a Billable party route
reverseFindings.explanation: Supersedes the 22 July billable-party rulings. The payer is one per Booking (parent, guardian, benefactor or family trust) and needs an email or postal address (28 October); 'there is no separate guardian record' (US-11.2.4). The prototype's New guardian sheet takes name, relationship and phone only, is per Procedure, office-only after add time, and tied to the Billable party route.
reverseFindings.verify_note: US-11.2.2, US-11.2.3 and US-11.2.4 read directly; createBillableParty takes name, relationshipToPatient, phone.

reverseFindings.title: Funding split is an office-only per-line editor, not a Booking action with typed dollars or percent
reverseFindings.explanation: Supersedes the 22 July per-line funder allocation. Any user presses a split on a Procedure's Contract line and types each party's share as $ or %; each party gets its own invoice; after the combined invoice is sent a split is credit and rebill (OQ-77). The prototype's editor is office-only, per billing line, amounts only.
reverseFindings.verify_note: US-08.2.3 text and ACs read directly ('a user action on the Booking', typed $ or %); sheet is rendered inside the office-only billing setup.

reverseFindings.title: Contracts are edited in place, deletable, and the billing monitor un-end-dates one to retry
reverseFindings.explanation: Supersedes Phase 08 contract maintenance and the S4 billing-failure beat. Each Contract is a series of dated versions, never backdated, never deleted, with changes staged and reviewed. The prototype edits terms in place, deletes unreferenced Contracts, and Resolve and retry clears an end date; the S4 demo action ends a Contract in the past.
reverseFindings.verify_note: US-04.2.10 ('nothing is backdated and nothing is deleted') read directly; US-04.1.6 is still Proposed (status 1) so the staged-review UI is a proposal, but the versioning rule is Agreed.

reverseFindings.title: The GST report lists customer receipts, not the payments passed to the anaesthetist
reverseFindings.explanation: Supersedes the 24 July GST-activity reading. US-12.2.2 lists the payments AA made to the anaesthetist in the month with the GST of each. The prototype lists receipts on the day the customer pays, before any payout, on mobile and web. The BCTI treatment is still open (OQ-29, OQ-47).
reverseFindings.verify_note: gstActivityFor filters state.billing.receipts; US-12.2.2 says 'payments AA made to the anaesthetist... not invoices sent'.

reverseFindings.title: Dashboard Productivity and Leave panels
reverseFindings.explanation: The dashboard summarises calendar, financial position and locum availability (US-12.2.3). Productivity tiles have no backing, and Leave rows (Approved, Pending) imply an approval workflow while availability is something the anaesthetist sets herself. Both are seeded for one persona, not derived.
reverseFindings.verify_note: US-12.2.3 read directly; no catalogue item mentions productivity tiles. Seed holds figures for Dr Souter only.

reverseFindings.title: Receivables ageing buckets, age chips and an Overdue view
reverseFindings.explanation: OQ-59 is answered: a flat list of unpaid payables, oldest first, no ageing buckets, no age chips, no Overdue view. Since 28 October each line links back to its Booking. The prototype has ageing bars, an Overdue tab with bucket columns and amber age chips, and rows open nothing.
reverseFindings.verify_note: US-12.2.1 read directly ('no ageing buckets and no age chips'; AC 'Back to the Booking').

reverseFindings.title: Prior balance tag has no threshold and sits on the billing monitor after authorisation
reverseFindings.explanation: The alert fires when a Booking is created or matched, for an invoice unpaid beyond a 90-day threshold from the invoice date (mild or strong, never blocking), and since 28 October the anaesthetist sees it on their List. The prototype tags any open prior episode with no threshold, only on the billing monitor after authorisation, and shows the anaesthetist nothing. The tag's own tooltip admits 'not yet distinguished'.
reverseFindings.verify_note: US-11.3.2 read directly (90 days from invoice date; mild vs strong; anaesthetist sees it on the Booking in their List).

reverseFindings.title: Review flag: ACC should not bill the patient directly
reverseFindings.explanation: An ACC-funded Procedure is an ordinary Procedure priced by the holder's ACC Contract; ACC is never billed directly and is invisible to the engine (US-05.5.1). The flag implies an ACC rule the engine does not have and is derived from the billing route, so it falls away with the route rework (RV-18). ACC chips on money lists are harmless.
reverseFindings.verify_note: US-05.5.1 read directly; flag condition is accRelated plus billingRoute billableParty.

reverseFindings.title: Modifier master is demo values and codes that differ from the transcribed RVG table
reverseFindings.explanation: The modifier master is the RVG table plus AA's own list, values as the RVG prints them (US-05.1.5, Agreed). The prototype's table is labelled demo-plausible and disagrees (AS3 is 3 vs RVG 2, invented AS2, PO1, PO2, PA1 to PA4 values, missing VM1, TTE1/2, PACU1, EAA1, POC codes), and age codes are ordinary chips rather than pre-applied from date of birth.
reverseFindings.verify_note: Compared against requirements-board/requirements/artifacts/files/NZSA RVG 2021 modifiers.md: AS3 = 2 there, 'No AS2 or ASA V code', VM1, TTE1, TTE2, PACU1, EAA1 and POC rows exist and are absent from modifierCodes.ts.

reverseSummary:
Adversarial pass at HEAD 7cd78025 (aa-prototype unchanged since d4db277; uncommitted tree ignored). Of 39 draft findings, 37 upheld, 1 corrected (RV-27) and 1 dropped (RV-17), leaving 38. I re-read the catalogue items cited by the 13 rewritten findings and RV-39, and re-checked the cited code lines. No findings were added: my extra checks found nothing clearly missed.

Dropped: RV-17 (photo of the booking card) is refuted. US-02.4.4 is Future Work, the Add a booking sheet opens on manual entry only (AddBookingFlow.tsx:38-58), and PhotoCaptureFlow is reachable only through the badged "Photo capture (Future scope)" demo action (registry.ts:997). Nothing misleads. The two table rows that pointed at it in reverse-check.md now say "Handled".

Corrected: RV-27 (office single-Booking move). US-01.4.7 and OQ-85 state the "free colleague, new List, never an existing List" rule for the anaesthetist's own move only. The office flow is an owner question, not a defect. The prototype has no anaesthetist-side single-Booking move at all, which is a gap item. The action changed from Rework to Keep as demo scaffold.

Upheld with notes:
- RV-05 and RV-24: confirmed against US-06.4.1, US-06.2.1, OQ-96, OQ-115 and OQ-116.
- RV-09: the catalogue itself splits on whether an included P1 is lockable. US-05.1.4 says not locked; US-03.3.4's first paragraph says it cannot be unselected.
- RV-08: US-05.3.3 was a merge, so the prototype really implements the old RFP split-billing rule. The kind is left as filed.
- RV-22: US-03.3.4 explicitly says nothing else is pre-filled "whatever the patient's ASA grade", but OQ-95 part 1 is formally open, so confidence stays moderate.
- RV-29: Donald's own decision, so confirm with him.
- RV-15: low-priority residue only.
- RV-38: checked against the transcribed RVG table (AS3 is 2, no AS2).
- RV-03: confirmed; the fixed ancillary billing lines also stay until Events replace them.

reverse-check.md is updated to match: header, Verification status, the two table rows, RV-17 section removed and the RV-27 action changed. All other sections are unchanged.
